title: Index routine preserves probabilistic semantics
statement: Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, $k$ one of the four index sites, and $\sigma$ a register state whose fifteen values are at most $B$. Write $r$ and $c$ for the values in the row and column positions specified by $k$, and suppose $r<n$ and $c<n$, where $n$ is the vertex-count register of $\sigma$. Assume $2n+2+2n^2\le B$, and that the program started at the entry specified by $k$ from the state obtained by setting its input pointer to $2n+2+2(rn+c)$ and its row and inner counters to $r,c$ has all live register values at most $B$, terminates along every sequence of choices, and has acceptance probability $q$ and rejection probability $1-q$ for every choice length at which every sequence of choices halts. Then the program started at the index routine for $k$ from $\sigma$ has those same bounded-register termination and probability properties.
hypotheses_covered: $\sigma$ is a register state bounded by $B$
the specified modified state at entry $\operatorname{ixEx}(k)$ has bounded-register probabilistic semantics $q$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, $k$ an index site,
and $\sigma$ a 15-register configuration. Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most
$B$, and let $r$ and $c$ be the values in the row and column registers specified by $k$;
assume $r<\sigma.n$, $c<\sigma.n$, and $2\sigma.n+2+2\sigma.n^2\le B$. If the program
started at the entry for $k$ with input pointer $2\sigma.n+2+2(r\sigma.n+c)$, row
register $r$, column register $c$, and all other registers as in $\sigma$ has
bounded-register termination and acceptance probability $q$ (and rejection probability
$1-q$) for every choice length at which every sequence of choices halts, then the
program started at the index routine for $k$ with configuration $\sigma$ has the same
bounded-register termination and probabilities.
